pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director. A psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: psalm: a song sung to music
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

records.heading: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}?

records.source: עַד־אָ֣נָה יְ֭הוָה תִּשְׁכָּחֵ֣נִי נֶ֑צַח עַד־אָ֓נָה׀תַּסְתִּ֖יר אֶת־פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: Until when, YHWH, will you forget me forever? Until when will you hide your face from me?
pieces: How long, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} go on forgetting me for good? How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face away from me?

L.2: Until when, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forget me forever? Until when will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face from me?

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep forgetting me? Will it be forever? How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} turn away and not look at me?

decisions.choice: Until when: How long
decisions.reason: The question ("until when?") is asked four times in verses 2-3. It is the cry of someone who has waited a long time (6:4; 74:10), not a request for a date.

decisions.choice: will you forget me forever?: two complaints in one
alternatives: How long? Will you forget me forever?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "how long" and "forever" in one question: it feels as though the LORD's forgetting will never end. Balanced splits it into two questions, which says the same.

decisions.choice: hide your face: withdraw favor and help
decisions.reason: God's face turned toward someone is his favor and help (4:7; Numbers 6:25-26); to hide it is to leave a person without that help (10:11; 27:9).

records.source: עַד־אָ֨נָה אָשִׁ֪ית עֵצ֡וֹת בְּנַפְשִׁ֗י יָג֣וֹן בִּלְבָבִ֣י יוֹמָ֑ם עַד־אָ֓נָה׀יָר֖וּם אֹיְבִ֣י עָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: Until when will I set counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day? Until when will be exalted my enemy over me?
pieces: How long must I keep turning plans over in my mind, with grief in my heart all day long? How long will my enemy stand over me in triumph?

L.3: Until when will I set counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart by day? Until when will my enemy be exalted over me?

R.3: How long must I keep worrying and trying to find a way out? How long will I feel sad every day? How long will my enemy keep winning against me?

decisions.choice: set counsels in my soul: keep making plans inside, with no way out
alternatives: bear pain in my soul (with a small change)
decisions.reason: To set counsels in the soul is to keep turning plans over in the mind, looking for a way out and finding none. Some suggest a small change that gives "pain" in place of "counsels"; the Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: by day: all day long
decisions.reason: The word (yomam) means in the daytime or day after day. Some ancient Greek manuscripts add "and night".

decisions.choice: be exalted over me: stand over me as the winner
decisions.reason: The verb means to be raised up: the enemy rises in triumph while the psalmist is brought low.

records.source: הַבִּ֣יטָֽה עֲ֭נֵנִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י הָאִ֥ירָה עֵ֝ינַ֗י פֶּן־אִישַׁ֥ן הַמָּֽוֶת׃
records.gloss: Look, answer me, YHWH my God; give light to my eyes, lest I sleep the death,
pieces: Turn and look, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, and answer me! Bring the light back to my eyes, or I will fall asleep in death,

L.4: Look, answer me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God; give light to my eyes, lest I sleep the [sleep of] death,

R.4: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, look at me and answer me! Make me strong again, or I will die.

decisions.choice: give light to my eyes: give me new life
decisions.reason: Bright eyes are a sign of strength and life; when Jonathan ate honey after a long fast, "his eyes brightened" (1 Samuel 14:27, 29). Dim eyes go with weakness and grief (6:8). The psalmist asks God to revive him.

decisions.choice: sleep the death: die
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a sleep (Jeremiah 51:39); the Hebrew says literally "lest I sleep the death".

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 5 ("lest my enemy say ..."), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: Make me strong again
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: פֶּן־יֹאמַ֣ר אֹיְבִ֣י יְכָלְתִּ֑יו צָרַ֥י יָ֝גִ֗ילוּ כִּ֣י אֶמּֽוֹט׃
records.gloss: lest says my enemy, I have prevailed over him; my foes rejoice because I am shaken.
pieces: and my enemy will say, "I have beaten him," and those against me will celebrate when I stumble.

L.5: lest my enemy say, "I have prevailed over him," [lest] my foes rejoice because I am shaken.

R.5: Then my enemy will say, "I won!" The people who are against me will be glad to see me fall.

decisions.choice: I am shaken: I totter and fall
decisions.reason: The verb (mot) is used of something that slips or gives way; here, the psalmist's fall. Psalm 15:5 and 16:8 use it for the one who is never shaken.

decisions.choice: lest: the fear behind the prayer
decisions.reason: The "lest" of verse 4 goes on: if God does not act, the enemy will gloat.

decisions.choice: and ... will
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what will happen if God does not act, which is the sense of "lest" here (m2).

records.source: וַאֲנִ֤י׀בְּחַסְדְּךָ֣ בָטַחְתִּי֮ יָ֤גֵ֥ל לִבִּ֗י בִּֽישׁוּעָ֫תֶ֥ךָאָשִׁ֥ירָה לַיהוָ֑ה כִּ֖י גָמַ֣ל עָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: But I, in your loyal love I have trusted; my heart will rejoice in your salvation; I will sing to YHWH, for he has dealt fully with me.
pieces: But I trust in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love; my heart will be glad because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save. I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been so generous to me.

L.6: But I, in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love I have trusted; my heart will rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation. I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has dealt fully with me.

R.6: But I trust in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. I will be full of joy when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me. I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been so kind to me.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps faith
decisions.reason: As in 5:8, the word (chesed) is love that stays loyal to a relationship and a promise.

decisions.choice: But I have trusted: the turn of the psalm
decisions.reason: "But I" sets the psalmist against the gloating enemy. The verb is in the past form: he has put his trust in God's love and it still holds, though nothing has yet changed. He then speaks of joy and singing as sure to come.

decisions.choice: dealt fully with me: treated me generously
decisions.reason: The verb (gamal) means to deal out in full, to repay; with God as subject, to treat someone with great kindness (116:7; 142:8).

decisions.choice: because you save (B); when you save me (R)
decisions.reason: The noun (yeshu'ah) is God's act of saving; Balanced and Readable use the verb.

decisions.choice: loyal love (B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.
